# Copilot Instructions for Sick Of It

Read all the .md files in the project root before making any changes.
Start with ARCHITECTURE.md, then CURRENT-STATE.md, then REFACTOR-PLAN-6.md.

## Critical Rules

### 1. GameDefinition is the Source of Truth
- Located at `Assets/Resources/GameDefinition.asset`
- Contains: LevelConfig[], VideoConfig[], DeathConfig[], EnemyTypeConfig[], PlayerConfig, ProjectileConfig[]
- **UI Scene Configs**: MainMenuConfig, SelectionSceneConfig (level/video), UpgradeShopConfig
- Runtime reads config; generators create assets from config
- **Never hardcode values that should come from config**
- **Dual-Update Rule**: When changing a default value (e.g., `spriteScale`), update BOTH:
  1. The C# field default in the config class (e.g., `spriteScale = 0.5f` in EnemyTypeConfig.cs) — for new entries
  2. All existing YAML entries in GameDefinition.asset (e.g., `spriteScale: 0.5` for each EnemyTypeConfig) — for existing entries

### 2. Everything is Generated
- **Prefabs** — Character.prefab, Enemy_*.prefab, Projectile_*.prefab, Diamond.prefab, Platform.prefab are generated
- **Animations** — All .controller and .anim files are generated by AnimationGenerator from AnimationConfig
- **Gameplay Scenes** — Video.unity, Level.unity, Death.unity generated by scene generators
- **UI Scenes** — MainMenu.unity, LevelSelection.unity, VideoSelection.unity, UpgradeShop.unity generated by UI scene generators
- **Never manually edit generated prefabs, scenes, or animation files** — edit configs and regenerate via `SickOfIt → Generate Project`
- **ONE BUTTON**: `SickOfIt → Generate Project` does everything — cleanup, prefabs, animations, scenes, addressables
- AnimationConfig is auto-populated by generators if null (based on EnemyType for enemies, hardcoded for player)
- Generation order: Projectiles → Pickups → Platforms → Player → Enemies → Gameplay Scenes → UI Scenes → Addressables

### 3. No Bypass Fields
- **No `animatorController` field** — generators ALWAYS create animations from config/spriteSheet
- **No `defaultSprite` field** — generators auto-detect first sprite from the sprite sheet
- Config is the ONLY source of truth. There are no "use this pre-made asset" escape hatches.

### 4. Generator Cleanup Before Regeneration
- Each generator deletes its output before creating new assets
- This ensures idempotency — running generation twice produces identical results
- Generators use `AssetDatabase.DeleteAsset()` for prefabs

### 5. Serialized References via SerializedObject
- All cross-object references are wired at generation time using `SerializedObject`
- **Never use GetComponent at runtime** — use `[SerializeField]` fields wired by generators
- Acceptable pattern: `if (field == null) field = GetComponent<T>()` as fallback only

### 6. Scene Architecture
- **7 generated scenes total**:
  - Gameplay: `Video.unity`, `Level.unity`, `Death.unity`
  - UI: `MainMenu.unity`, `LevelSelection.unity`, `VideoSelection.unity`, `UpgradeShop.unity`
- Scene names are exact — runtime checks `scene.name == "Video"`, etc.
- **Never create individual scenes** like Video1, Level2 — config-driven through same scenes

### 7. PlayerPrefs Bridge
- SceneTransitionManager sets PlayerPrefs before loading a scene
- Runtime reads PlayerPrefs to know which config to use (level number, video number, death name)
- Example: `PlayerPrefs.SetInt("CurrentLevelNumber", 3)` → LevelRuntime reads it in Start()

### 8. No Runtime Scene Lookups
- **Never use**: `GameObject.Find`, `FindObjectOfType`, `FindObjectsOfType`, `FindGameObjectWithTag`
- All references assigned via serialized fields or injection methods like `SetPlayer()`, `SetProjectilePool()`
- One exception: `GameObject.Find(path)` in ExperienceRunner for config-driven named object activation

### 9. Object Pool System
- Projectiles use ObjectPool, not Instantiate/Destroy
- Pools are created by LevelSceneGenerator and wired to LevelRuntime
- LevelRuntime distributes pools to PlayerController and enemies via `SetProjectilePool()`/`SetLaserPool()`
- On rewind, RewindTimeline calls `ReturnAllPools()` — no projectile Destroy during rewind

### 10. Rewind System
- Component-based: RewindableTransform, RewindableRigidbody2D, RewindableGameObject, RewindableHealth, RewindableAnimator
- All rewindable objects need these components pre-attached (by generators)
- Components self-register with RewindTimeline in Awake
- Awake/OnDestroy registration (not OnEnable/OnDisable) — dead objects stay registered for revival

### 11. Assembly Structure
| Assembly | Contents |
|----------|----------|
| SickOfIt.Data | GameDefinition, all config types |
| SickOfIt.Core | GameClock, ObjectPool, Rewind system, Input |
| SickOfIt.Core.Progression | VideoRuntime, LevelRuntime, DeathRuntime |
| SickOfIt.Combat | EnemyBase, Health systems, Damage |
| SickOfIt.Tools.Editor | All generators, build tools |

## Unity Best Practices

### Code Patterns
```csharp
// ✅ GOOD: Serialized field with fallback
[SerializeField] private Rigidbody2D rb;
private void Awake() { if (rb == null) rb = GetComponent<Rigidbody2D>(); }

// ❌ BAD: Runtime lookup
private void Start() { rb = FindObjectOfType<Rigidbody2D>(); }

// ✅ GOOD: Injection method
public void SetPlayer(Transform player, IDamageable damageable) { ... }

// ❌ BAD: Tag lookup
player = GameObject.FindGameObjectWithTag("Player").transform;

// ✅ GOOD: Pool-based spawning
var projectile = projectilePool.Get(position, rotation);

// ❌ BAD: Direct instantiate for poolable objects
Instantiate(projectilePrefab, position, rotation);
```

### Generator Patterns
```csharp
// ✅ GOOD: Wire serialized fields via SerializedObject
var so = new SerializedObject(component);
so.FindProperty("targetField").objectReferenceValue = value;
so.ApplyModifiedPropertiesWithoutUndo();

// ❌ BAD: Assume Unity will wire references
component.targetField = value;  // Won't persist in prefab!
```

### Config Patterns
```csharp
// ✅ GOOD: Read from config
var config = GameDefinition.Instance.GetLevel(levelNumber);
moveSpeed = config.playerMoveSpeed;

// ❌ BAD: Hardcoded values
moveSpeed = 5f;
```

### Animation Patterns
```csharp
// ✅ GOOD: Define animation via AnimationConfig on EnemyTypeConfig/PlayerConfig
//   Parameters, states, transitions, events — all in config
//   AnimationGenerator creates .controller + .anim files from config
//   AnimationConfig is auto-populated by generators when null — just run: SickOfIt → Generate Project

// ❌ BAD: Manually create .controller or .anim files
//   These will be deleted on next generation

// ✅ GOOD: Simple looping animation — just set spriteSheet on config (no AnimationConfig needed)
//   Generator auto-creates a single idle clip via AnimationGenerator.GenerateSimpleIdle()

// ❌ BAD: Reference animation assets directly — they are regenerated each build
```

## File Organization

```
Assets/
├── Animations/
│   ├── Enemies/                 ← GENERATED by AnimationGenerator (via EnemyPrefabGenerator)
│   ├── Player/                  ← GENERATED by AnimationGenerator (via PlayerPrefabGenerator)
│   ├── Projectiles/             ← GENERATED by AnimationGenerator (via ProjectilePrefabGenerator)
│   └── Pickups/                 ← GENERATED by AnimationGenerator (via PickupPrefabGenerator)
├── Prefabs/
│   ├── Character.prefab         ← GENERATED by PlayerPrefabGenerator
│   ├── Diamond.prefab           ← GENERATED by PickupPrefabGenerator
│   ├── Platform.prefab          ← GENERATED by PlatformPrefabGenerator
│   └── Combat/
│       ├── Enemy_*.prefab       ← GENERATED by EnemyPrefabGenerator
│       └── Projectile_*.prefab  ← GENERATED by ProjectilePrefabGenerator
├── Resources/
│   ├── GameDefinition.asset     ← MANUAL (edited by humans/AI)
│   └──           ← MANUAL (edited by humans/AI)
├── Scenes/
│   ├── Video.unity, Level.unity, Death.unity  ← GENERATED
│   └── MainMenu.unity, etc.     ← GENERATED (UI scene generators)
└── Scripts/
    └── Tools/Editor/Generation/  ← All generators live here
```
